subject: oop
question: Which access specifier allows a class member to be accessed only within its own class?
title: The Diary Lock
hook: Your diary is locked in your own room. Which keyword is that?
answer: The answer is the private access specifier.
A private member is accessible only within its own class.
No other class can use it, not even a subclass; outsiders must go through public methods.
Order of openness: public > protected > default > private.
